page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The server includes 16.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), 48 MB of L3 cache, and extended instruction set support including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, and SHA_NI. It operates without local disk storage or GPU hardware, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent average performance across standard single-core and multi-core CPU workloads, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark tests. Static web serving throughput and Redis operations also perform within middle-tier expectations. However, hardware benchmarks reveal a tradeoff in memory subsystem efficiency: while small cached memory reads are baseline, uncached memory bandwidth falls into lower percentiles, contributing to weak overall PassMark memory scores and reduced performance during medium 7B model LLM inference.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM resource ratio, the ecs.c7.2xlarge offers dedicated compute allocation suitable for processing tasks that do not depend heavily on high memory bandwidth per core. The server fits workloads such as web application serving, software compilation, bzip3 data decompression, and moderate database operations. Workloads bound by uncached memory throughput or large LLM context windows may encounter execution bottlenecks on this profile.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.2xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it features 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 16.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core), 48 MB of L3 cache, and a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached volumes. Benchmarks demonstrate steady average performance in single-core and multi-core CPU operations, software compilation, web serving, and Redis execution. However, uncached memory bandwidth and 7B model LLM inference score in lower performance percentiles, marking a key hardware tradeoff. This configuration fits CPU-focused tasks, web serving, and build jobs rather than memory-bandwidth-heavy applications.
